newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU TO FORCE VAT ON FOREIGN TELECOMS FIRMS.
newsitem.headline: EU TO FORCE VAT ON FOREIGN TELECOMS FIRMS.

text.p: The European Commission will go ahead on Wednesday with rules to force non-EU telecommunications firms to charge VAT on services offered in the 15-nation bloc.

The move follows a unanimous request by national governments anxious to defend their own telecoms operators from unfair competition and to preserve tax revenue at a time when every effort is required to meet tough budgetary criteria for the EU's single currency.
Under an existing directive on Value Added Tax on telecoms services, companies based outside the Union do not have to levy VAT on their European clients.
But both the European industry and national capitals argue that the rules, adopted in 1977, no longer correspond to the reality of the telecoms market which has become increasingly global.

They are particularly concerned about the development of so-called "call-back" services, by which companies and individials can dial a number, usually in the United States, and get called back with an open line to phone anywhere in the world without going through the local operator. International calls made through such services or by using calling cards are usually much cheaper, partly because they avoid VAT.
The Commission on Wednesday will agree derogations valid two years which will make European purchasers of such services, rather than the foreign service providers, liable for the tax.

This is until the 1977 directive is properly revised, which should happen by 1999 at the latest, at which point non-EU telecoms firms would have to register for VAT in at least an EU country, Commission officials said.

European operators, such as British Telecommunications Plc, complained at a meeting with Commission taxation officials earlier this month that the provisional rules were far from removing all the distortions in competition.
But the Commission's draft has not been changed, one Commission source said on Tuesday.
